lead.headline: Barkley and Rice hurt, no diagnosis; a tight end needed by Wednesday
lead.deck: Finished at 63.7 to Team 13's 70.5 with Pitts to come. Fifty points sat on the bench. Rice and Waller are both off in Week 5.
lead.body: Two hamstrings decided it and neither has a diagnosis. Saquon Barkley was hurt on his second carry, four snaps into the Rams game; Rashee Rice pulled up after one catch in Las Vegas. Between them they scored 2.0. By Monday morning there was no scan result for either, only a reporter who saw Barkley walking normally and another who says Rice could miss several weeks. Rice was going to sit in Week 5 anyway, since Kansas City are on bye, and so is Darren Waller, who had six targets and 6.6 in Carolina's win. The healthy starters didn't cover the gap: Garrett Wilson's Jets held the ball for 17 minutes, and Josh Downs drew four targets in a game the Colts led throughout. Jonathan Taylor's 22.7 was the exception. You finished on 63.68. Team 13 started two inactive players, have 70.52, and still have Kyle Pitts tonight. On your bench Carnell Tate caught nine of 12 targets for 145 yards and 21.5, Ollie Gordon ran for 100 and 18.0, and Matthew Golden and Bhayshul Tuten added 22.8 between them. No brief benched them; the projection did. Next week the receivers on that bench step in for Rice. The tight-end slot has nobody, three candidates sit on waivers until 01:00 on Wednesday, and tomorrow's brief has to pick one and find him a seat.
